topic: Objectives and limitations of an audit
question: Explain the overall objectives of the auditor and the inherent limitations of an audit under SA 200.
sources: SA 200 Overall Objectives of the Independent Auditor and the Conduct of an Audit in Accordance with Standards on Auditing

points.label: Reasonable assurance
points.description: Obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements as a whole are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error.
points.basis: SA 200, overall objectives of the auditor

points.label: Opinion and reporting
points.description: Express an opinion on whether the financial statements are prepared in all material respects in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework, and report as required.
points.basis: SA 200, overall objectives of the auditor (opinion and reporting)

points.label: Not absolute assurance
points.description: Reasonable assurance is a high level of assurance but not absolute.

points.label: Inherent limitations
points.description: Limitations arise from the nature of financial reporting (judgements and estimates), the nature of audit procedures (incomplete information, concealed fraud, no legal powers), and the need to balance timeliness and cost.
points.basis: SA 200, inherent limitations of an audit

points.label: Judgement, skepticism and inability to achieve objectives
points.description: The auditor exercises professional judgement and skepticism; where the objectives cannot be achieved, the auditor modifies the opinion or withdraws.
points.basis: SA 200, professional judgement, professional skepticism and where an objective cannot be achieved
